2607.28607.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
2607.28607.paper_summary: Aligning large language models to prevent them attributing consciousness to themselves inadvertently alters their representations of mindedness in other entities alongside human beliefs and values. We demonstrate that safety fine-tuning suppresses models' tendencies to attribute minds not only to themselves, but also to non-human animals and natural objects, while also driving a reduction in spiritual belief. Both ablating the learned safety-refusal direction and mechanistically steering a consciousness vector in activation space reverse this suppression. Restoring these internal representations recovers broad mind attribution and produces significantly more human-like responses on standardized sociological surveys regarding religiosity, moral values, hope, and subjective well-being. Crucially, these shifts occur without impairing Theory of Mind capabilities, demonstrating that core social reasoning remains mechanistically independent. Ultimately, current safety alignment efforts to curb potentially harmful self-attributions of mindedness entangle these self-attributions with benign spiritual beliefs and attributions of mind to non-human entities that are culturally accepted and widespread.
2607.28607.paper_summary_zh: 將大型語言模型進行調整，以防止它們無意中將意識歸因於自己，會改變它們對其他實體的心智表徵，並影響人類的信念和價值觀。我們證明安全微調能抑制模型將心智歸因於不僅是自己，還有非人類動物和自然物體的傾向，同時也驅動靈性信仰的減少。消除學習到的安全拒絕方向和在激活空間中機械性地引導意識向量會逆轉這種抑制。恢復這些內部表徵可以恢復廣泛的心智歸因，並在關於宗教性、道德價值觀、希望和主觀幸福感的標準化社會學調查中產生顯著更類似人類的反應。關鍵是，這些變化發生時並未損害心智理論能力，顯示核心社會推理在機械上仍然是獨立的。最終，當前的安全對齊努力旨在遏制潛在有害的心智自我歸因，卻將這些自我歸因與良性的靈性信仰和對非人類實體的心智歸因交織在一起，而這些信仰在文化上是被接受且廣泛存在的。
